texts.preamble: Vappancheri Sreedharan vs The Food Inspector on 7 January, 2016 Author: B.Sudheendra Kumar Bench: B.Sudheendra Kumar In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present: The Honourable Mr. Justice B.Sudheendra Kumar Thursday, The 7Th Day Of January 2016/17Th Pousha, 1937 Crl.Rev.Pet.No. 2541 of 2007 ( ) --------------------------------- Crl.A 326/2006 of Sessions Court,Kozhikode Cc 122/2006 of Spl.J.M.F.C. For Trial Of Maradu Cases, Kozhikode Revision Petitioner(S)/Appellant/Accused:: -------------------------------------------------------------------- Vappancheri Sreedharan, Aged 59 Years, S/O.Late Velukutty, 21/1348, Chakkumkadavu P.O.Kallai, Calicut, Residing At Vappancheri House P.O.Nallalam, Calicut. By Advs.Sri.R.Sudhish Sri.P.P.Balan Respondent(S)/Respondents/Complainant And State;: ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 1. The Food Inspector, Calicut Corporation. 2. State Of Kerala Represented By The Public Prosecutor, High Court Of Kerala, Ernakulam. By Public Prosecutor, Shri.R.Githesh This Criminal Revision Petition Having Been Finally Heard On 07-01-2016, The Court On The Same Day Passed The Following: Vappancheri Sreedharan vs The Food Inspector on 7 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13365928/ 1 B.Sudheendra Kumar, J. - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -- - - -- - - - - - - - - - -- - - - - - - - - Crl.R.P. No.2541 of 2007 - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - Dated this the 7th day of January 2016 O R D E R
texts.facts: The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:- On 20.7.2005 at about 12.30 p.m., PW1, the Food Inspector, Kozhikode Corporation, purchased pickle from the shop of the revision petitioner. After sampling as per rules, one of the samples was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst. The Public Analyst filed Ext. P10 report stating that the food item did not conform to the standard prescribed for pickles. It was reported that the constituents were not within the prescribed limits. It was further reported that the colouring matters were added to the pickles against the provisions of the law and therefore, the same was adulterated. 4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW4 were examined and Exts. P1 to P18 were marked for the prosecution. No evidence was adduced on the side of the revision petitioner.
texts.arguments: 5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. P10 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument. 6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was specified as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act. Therefore, Ext. P10 report of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case was adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra). It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal. In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the Vappancheri Sreedharan vs The Food Inspector on 7 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13365928/ 2 accused. The matter was referred to a Division Bench and the Division Bench also affirmed the said decision, submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
